scene.note: You write the lines of first_line.py, Python runs them from top to bottom, and the terminal shows what they print.

steps.note: Rhona wants the team's name printed, exactly as the task spells it.
Under Task 1 you add one line that prints it, with the text in quotes.
Python reads the file from the top and runs each line in turn.
The team's name shows up on a line of its own in the terminal.
The radio check has two lines, and Rhona wants them in the order the task gives.
Each line of the radio check gets its own print, one under the other.
Python runs the two prints in the order they are written.
The terminal shows the two lines, one right after the other.
A line under Task 3 still sends people to the old base the team has left.
Python skips every line that is a comment.
The old meeting place no longer prints, and the line stays in the file in case Rhona wants it back.
A comment is a note for the next person who opens the file, like Rhona.
Python skips comments, so your note changes nothing that runs.
The terminal prints the same lines as before your note.
